nodes.rationale: Concrete algorithmic hardness (discrete log, LWE, SHA collision resistance). SNARKs with knowledge soundness resist falsifiable-assumption constructions because a short proof cannot obviously yield a long witness; SNARGs for subclasses (batch NP, deterministic computation) are achievable.

nodes.label: Correlation Intractability
nodes.author: Alex Lombardi
nodes.rationale: Hard to find x with h(x)=f(x). Impossible for unrestricted input lengths (diagonalization: feed h its own description), so constructions bound input length and the running time of f; the FHE/LWE construction hides a trap function g* = Dec(f(x))+1 inside the hash key. Suffices to instantiate Fiat-Shamir for statistically (round-by-round) sound protocols by making bad challenges unreachable.

nodes.label: Random Oracle Model
nodes.author: Alex Lombardi
nodes.rationale: Assumes attacks treat the hash as a black box; provably violated by correlation-intractability diagonalization and by the Barak / Goldwasser-Kalai protocols where Fiat-Shamir is ROM-secure yet insecure for every concrete hash. Recursive SNARKs run the hash on (something like) its own description, so the secure/insecure line is genuinely unclear.

nodes.label: Somewhere Statistically Binding Commitment
nodes.author: Alex Lombardi
nodes.rationale: Hash key can be sampled to statistically bind one hidden coordinate of the committed vector, and the modes are indistinguishable; makes the batch-NP protocol statistically sound on any single false statement, which is exactly the hook correlation intractability needs.

nodes.label: Parallel Repetition of ZK Protocols
nodes.author: Alex Lombardi
nodes.rationale: Reduces soundness error for statistically sound protocols but does not preserve zero knowledge: Dwork-Naor-Reingold-Stockmeyer show either Fiat-Shamir fails for the repeated 3-coloring protocol or the protocol is not ZK against malicious verifiers.

nodes.label: Recursive SNARK (Proof of a Proof)
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.rationale: Prove knowledge of a proof rather than the witness: enables proof compression (fast inner prover + short outer proof), streaming proof generation for rollups, and prover markets. Extractor composition forces recursion depth to be logarithmic, and random-oracle gates in the verifier must be instantiated with a concrete hash (e.g. Poseidon) before recursion, at the cost of an extra assumption.

nodes.label: Additively Homomorphic Commitment
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.rationale: com(m1)+com(m2)=com(m1+m2); required so the folding verifier can fold committed error vectors it never sees (e.g. Pedersen commitments).

nodes.label: Field Emulation
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.rationale: Implements Fq arithmetic as a circuit over Fp; correct but blows up the verifier circuit (e.g. pairing checks), making the recursive prover very slow.

nodes.label: Pasta Curves (Pallas and Vesta)
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.rationale: Type-III two-cycle (no pairings) built from y^2=x^3+5 via the Silverman-Stange theorem; designed for Halo2 recursion with non-pairing polynomial commitments.

nodes.label: Sangria
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.rationale: Observes Nova's folding applies to any quadratic constraint system, so Plonk arithmetization can be folded directly, giving smaller witnesses.

nodes.label: SuperNova
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.rationale: Extends Nova to chains mixing multiple functions F1..Fk instead of one repeated F.

nodes.label: MOOC Lecture 10: Recursive SNARKs, IVC, and Folding Schemes
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.norm_label: mooc lecture 10: recursive snarks, ivc, and folding schemes

nodes.label: Cycles of Elliptic Curves
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.rationale: Two curves where the order of each equals the base field of the other let recursion ping-pong between groups so prover and verifier arithmetic always match, avoiding the huge circuits of field emulation; a group of order p over Fp is impossible (discrete log is easy).

nodes.label: Folding Scheme
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.rationale: Compresses two instances into one via a random linear combination so only a single folded instance ever needs a SNARK; replaces running the whole verifier circuit inside recursion with just two group multiplications plus hashing.

nodes.label: Incrementally Verifiable Computation (IVC)
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.rationale: Each step outputs the new state plus a proof that the step is correct AND that the previous proof verified; iterated extraction recovers the whole trace. Lets a prover handle arbitrarily long computations (a microprocessor stepped repeatedly) with memory bounded by one step - used for succinct blockchain state proofs and VDFs.

nodes.label: Relaxed R1CS
nodes.author: Dan Boneh
nodes.rationale: Adds a scalar c and error vector E (Az o Bz = c*Dz + E) so random linear combinations of R1CS instances stay in the language; E is replaced by an additively homomorphic commitment to keep instances succinct for the verifier.

nodes.label: Polynomial Commitment Scheme
nodes.author: Justin Thaler
nodes.rationale: Lets the prover commit to a large polynomial with a single hash/group element and later prove evaluations, so a polynomial IOP can run succinctly. The SNARK inherits transparency and post-quantum status entirely from the commitment scheme.

nodes.label: MOOC Lecture 8: FRI Polynomial Commitments and the Fiat-Shamir Transformation
nodes.author: Justin Thaler
nodes.norm_label: mooc lecture 8: fri polynomial commitments and the fiat-shamir transformation

nodes.label: Fiat-Shamir Transformation
nodes.author: Justin Thaler
nodes.rationale: Replaces verifier randomness with a hash of the transcript to make protocols non-interactive. Public input x must be hashed for adaptive security (a recurring deployment bug). Applying it to many-round protocols can be catastrophically insecure unless the protocol is round-by-round sound; non-interactive deployment demands far higher security levels because grinding is silent.

nodes.label: FRI Polynomial Commitment Scheme
nodes.author: Justin Thaler
nodes.rationale: Hash-based, transparent, plausibly post-quantum; shortest evaluation proofs among hashing-based schemes. Blowup factor rho^-1 trades prover time (grows linearly) against proof size/verification (falls logarithmically). Only ~0.5*log(1/rho) bits of security per query are provable; deployments assume the conjectured log(1/rho) bits, which a simple interpolation attack shows is tight.

nodes.label: Grinding Attack on Fiat-Shamir
nodes.author: Justin Thaler
nodes.rationale: Attacker iterates first messages until one hashes to a lucky challenge: 2^b hashes succeed with probability 2^(b-lambda), linearly better than birthday-style attacks; motivates >=128-bit security since 2^80 hashes/hour are feasible (Bitcoin network).

nodes.label: KZG Polynomial Commitments
nodes.author: Justin Thaler
nodes.rationale: Constant-size commitments and evaluation proofs via pairing-friendly groups; best known verification costs, but requires a trusted setup and is not post-quantum.

nodes.label: List Polynomial Commitment
nodes.author: Justin Thaler
nodes.rationale: Binds the prover to a small set of low-degree polynomials rather than a unique one; still suffices for SNARK security and lets FRI deployments claim log(1/rho) bits per query instead of operating inside the unique decoding radius.

nodes.label: Multiplicative Subgroup of n-th Roots of Unity
nodes.author: Justin Thaler
nodes.norm_label: multiplicative subgroup of n-th roots of unity
nodes.rationale: The squaring map is 2-to-1 on the n-th roots of unity (n even), halving the evaluation domain at each FRI fold; requires n | p-1, which is why FRI fields like Goldilocks (2^64-2^32+1) have large power-of-two subgroups.

nodes.label: Round-by-Round Soundness
nodes.author: Justin Thaler
nodes.rationale: Ensures a cheating prover must get lucky all at once in a single round, ruling out the per-round grinding that makes Fiat-Shamir on sequentially-repeated protocols totally insecure; known for sum-check and Bulletproofs but not yet published for FRI.

nodes.label: Proof Aggregation Circuit
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: Second-layer circuit proving all subcircuit proofs valid so only one proof is verified on L1; kept very thin (few columns) since verification cost is linear in columns.

nodes.label: EVM Circuit (State Machine Circuit)
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: Per-step witness = step context + one-hot case switch + opcode-specific cells; 256-bit words split into 8-bit limbs; ~100 columns and 2000+ custom gates.

nodes.label: Proof of Exploit
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: Make the transaction a private input: prove 'I know a transaction moving the state root to one where your balance is zero' - demonstrating a bug without revealing it.

nodes.label: zk-Oracle / zk Coprocessor Attestation
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: Trustlessly read historical on-chain data via zkEVM state proofs, compute over it off-chain, and verify the result on-chain (e.g. Axiom).

nodes.label: zk-Rollup
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: Layer-2 executes transactions off-chain and posts one succinct validity proof to L1, so L1 verifies a proof instead of re-executing every transaction.

nodes.author: Ye Zhang

nodes.label: GPU Prover Acceleration
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: MSM, NTT and quotient kernels parallelize well (30s EVM-circuit proofs), but then witness generation and CPU-to-GPU data copy dominate - a long-tail bottleneck that pure kernel acceleration cannot fix; peak memory cut from ~1TB to ~300GB CPU / 8GB GPU.

nodes.label: Halo2-KZG Proof System
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: Halo2's Plonkish front end with KZG (BN curve) replacing IPA/Pasta so proofs verify cheaply on Ethereum precompiles; used in both Scroll layers, with thin few-column aggregation tables and Poseidon-for-inner / Keccak-for-outer Fiat-Shamir hashing.

nodes.label: Lookup Argument / Lookup Tables
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: Prove a tuple belongs to a table: brute-force tables give cheap range and bitwise checks, dynamically generated tables give RAM consistency and hash outsourcing (Keccak table), and lookups are the glue connecting the zkEVM's subcircuits.

nodes.label: Plonkish Arithmetization
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: Chosen over R1CS because custom gates plus case-switch selectors handle the EVM's dynamic execution trace (open different opcode constraints per step) and lookups give cheap range proofs, RAM read/write consistency, and linking between subcircuits.

nodes.label: Random Linear Combination (RLC) Encoding
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: Compresses 32 8-bit limbs of an EVM word (and multi-cell lookup tuples) into one field element; sound only if the randomness is derived after the limbs are fixed, forcing the multi-phase Challenge API and pushing all subcircuits into one super circuit.

nodes.label: zkEVM
nodes.author: Ye Zhang
nodes.rationale: Proves batches of EVM transactions at the bytecode level so Solidity developers never write circuits and cross-app composability is preserved; became practical (~3 orders of magnitude) through flexible arithmetization (custom gates + lookups), hardware-accelerated provers, and recursive aggregation. Classified as language-, bytecode-, or consensus-level depending on compatibility depth.

nodes.label: Abstract Interpretation
nodes.author: Yu Feng
nodes.rationale: Computes conservative over-approximations of program state to detect known vulnerability patterns (re-entrancy, overflow) without specifications; imprecise abstractions yield false positives/negatives.

nodes.label: Circuit Dependence Graph
nodes.author: Yu Feng
nodes.rationale: Graph abstraction of a circuit: signal nodes with data-dependency and constraint edges; vulnerability detection becomes datalog queries over the graph (e.g. output signal with no constant or input constraint path).

nodes.label: Formal Verification
nodes.author: Yu Feng
nodes.rationale: Proves code matches a formal specification via VC generation and theorem provers; strongest guarantee, but needs manual specs and existing SMT solvers struggle with non-linear arithmetic over large prime fields ubiquitous in ZK circuits.

nodes.label: Vanguard Static Analysis Framework
nodes.author: Yu Feng
nodes.rationale: Compiles Circom/Halo2 circuits to circuit dependence graphs and runs pattern queries; found 32 previously unknown vulnerabilities across 258 circuits from 17 ZK projects.

nodes.label: MOOC Lecture 14: Securing ZK Circuits with Formal Methods (Veridise)
nodes.author: Yu Feng
nodes.norm_label: mooc lecture 14: securing zk circuits with formal methods (veridise)

nodes.label: Picus Verifier
nodes.author: Yu Feng
nodes.rationale: Verifies circuits are well-constrained by alternating a scalable static-analysis phase (grows the proven-constrained signal set) with a precise SMT phase in a loop; outperforms either technique alone because finite-field SMT solvers choke past a few hundred constraints.

nodes.label: Under-Constrained Circuit Bugs
nodes.author: Yu Feng
nodes.rationale: The constraint system accepts (x,y) pairs the witness computation would reject, letting attackers forge accepted proofs (drain funds, double spend). Examples: Num2Bits off-by-one leaving an output signal unconstrained, unconstrained LessThan output in a withdraw gadget, division-by-zero admitted when division is encoded as multiplication. Over-constrained bugs are rare because in-circuit assertions surface them during development.

nodes.label: Linear PCP
nodes.author: Yupeng Zhang
nodes.rationale: Oracle is a linear function (vector); verifier submits linear queries answered by inner products. Predates polynomial IOPs and underlies the earliest practical SNARK implementations.

nodes.label: Pinocchio (PGHR13)
nodes.author: Yupeng Zhang
nodes.rationale: One of the earliest efficient SNARK systems: 5-element proofs from QAP + bilinear pairings, with KOE-based consistency checks and public-input splitting.

nodes.label: Selector Polynomials
nodes.author: Yupeng Zhang
nodes.rationale: Interpolated over roots of unity to select the left/right inputs and output of each multiplication gate; addition gates are handled implicitly inside the summations.

nodes.label: MOOC Lecture 9: SNARKs from Linear PCPs and Quadratic Arithmetic Programs
nodes.author: Yupeng Zhang
nodes.norm_label: mooc lecture 9: snarks from linear pcps and quadratic arithmetic programs

nodes.label: Circuit-Specific Trusted Setup
nodes.author: Yupeng Zhang
nodes.rationale: Proving/verification keys embed selector polynomial evaluations at a secret tau that must be destroyed; the setup must be re-run for every new circuit, unlike Plonk/Marlin's universal setup.

nodes.label: Groth16 SNARK
nodes.author: Yupeng Zhang
nodes.rationale: Smallest known proofs (3 group elements, ~144 bytes) and one pairing-equation verification under the generic group model; the price is a circuit-specific trusted setup, a relatively slow FFT+multiexponentiation prover, and no post-quantum security.

nodes.label: Quadratic Arithmetic Program (QAP)
nodes.author: Yupeng Zhang
nodes.rationale: Reduces circuit satisfiability to one polynomial identity: L(x)*R(x)-O(x) divisible by the vanishing polynomial. Selector tables are public, sparse, and circuit-derived, so keys are generated in linear time; addition gates are absorbed into the selector sums for free. GGPR13's QAP cut prover cost from quadratic to quasi-linear, enabling Pinocchio and Groth16.

nodes.label: Rank-1 Constraint System (R1CS)
nodes.author: Yupeng Zhang
nodes.rationale: Generalizes 0/1 selector values to arbitrary public constants, so each constraint is (linear combo)*(linear combo)=(linear combo); additions and multiplications by constants are nearly free, and the matrix view (Az o Bz = Cz) underlies Spartan, Marlin, Bulletproofs and Nova.

nodes.norm_label: zk as a utility layer for verifiable claims

nodes.label: SP1 Hypercube zkVM
nodes.rationale: Rebuilt on multilinear polynomials because multilinears tile like rectangles with no wasted space (vs univariate spheres), so packing efficiency becomes prover speed; proves 93% of Ethereum mainnet blocks under 12s, ~5x over SP1 Turbo with ~2x fewer GPUs.

nodes.label: EF L1 zkEVM security foundations initiative
nodes.norm_label: ef l1 zkevm security foundations initiative
nodes.rationale: After the performance sprint (16 min -> 16 s latency, 45x cost drop, 99% of blocks under 10 s), security is the elephant in the room; the strategy is to lock security targets now so architectures stabilize enough for formal verification by H-star.

nodes.label: 128-bit provable security target
nodes.rationale: STARK conjectures are being mathematically disproven, silently shaving advertised bits (100 may really be 80); a soundness break lets an attacker forge anything - mint tokens, rewrite state, steal funds - so for an L1 zkEVM the margin is non-negotiable; 128 bits matches standardization-body recommendations.

nodes.norm_label: zkevm recursion architecture and its soundness
nodes.rationale: Modern zkEVMs compose many circuits with recursion in custom ways with lots of glue; documenting each team's topology and its soundness is essential for whole-system security.

nodes.label: Compact smart contract language
nodes.rationale: Bounded by design - fixed-size types, constant-bounded loops, no recursion - because every program must compile into finite proving circuits; strongly and statically typed unlike TypeScript; compiles to JavaScript plus TypeScript definitions, zkir proving circuits with keys, and a JSON contract-info file.

nodes.label: Compact witnesses (private-state callbacks)
nodes.rationale: Witness implementations are supplied by the TypeScript DApp, so a contract must never assume the code is its own: witness results are untrusted input.

nodes.label: Midnight Network
nodes.rationale: Privacy-first blockchain blending public verifiability with confidential data handling: verify correctness without revealing data, share only user-chosen disclosures, prove compliance while keeping records confidential.

nodes.label: Canton Network
nodes.rationale: Public permissionless blockchain purpose-built for institutional finance, combining privacy, compliance and scalability; governed by the Canton Foundation, powered by Canton Coin.

nodes.label: Tokenization of DTC-custodied U.S. Treasury securities
nodes.norm_label: tokenization of dtc-custodied u.s. treasury securities
nodes.rationale: First step of DTCC's strategy to hold securities on-chain following an SEC No-Action Letter; MVP in controlled production during H1 2026, phased to balance decentralized technology adoption with regulatory requirements.

nodes.label: Explicit disclosure / disclose() wrapper
nodes.rationale: Privacy is the default and disclosure the exception: any witness-derived data flowing to public state or exported returns must be wrapped in disclose(); the wrapper causes no disclosure itself, only acknowledges it, and should be placed after obfuscation such as hashing.

nodes.label: Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT)
nodes.rationale: The log's binding promise to incorporate a certificate within the Maximum Merge Delay; violating it is publicly provable misbehavior.

nodes.label: Signed Tree Head (STH)
nodes.rationale: Signed root plus tree size and timestamp; gossiped STHs let everyone detect a log presenting conflicting views (split-view attack).

nodes.label: Certificate Transparency
nodes.rationale: Publicly auditable, append-only, untrusted logs do not prevent certificate misissuance but guarantee its detection: interested parties monitor logs, and Merkle trees replace blind trust with efficiently checkable consistency. Eventually clients refuse unlogged certificates, forcing CAs to log everything.

nodes.label: Merkle Audit Path
nodes.rationale: Shortest list of additional nodes needed to compute the root from a leaf; a matching root proves the leaf exists in the tree.

nodes.label: Merkle Consistency Proof
nodes.rationale: Proves the append-only property between two tree heads with at most ceil(log2(n))+1 nodes, so auditors verify updates without holding the whole log.

nodes.label: Merkle Hash Tree
nodes.rationale: Binary SHA-256 tree with domain separation between leaf and node hashes for second-preimage resistance; the append-only property of a log is technically achieved by showing any version is a superset of any previous version.

nodes.label: Real-Time zkVMs
nodes.rationale: Real-time zkVMs replace EVM re-execution for lean execution, enabling full chain verification in every browser, wallet, and phone.

nodes.label: Danksharding
nodes.rationale: Makes L2 rollups much cheaper by adding blobs of data to Ethereum blocks; shard chains were dropped from the roadmap because rollups plus blob data scaled faster than expected.

nodes.label: PeerDAS
nodes.rationale: Peer-to-peer data availability sampling (shipped in Fusaka) enables more efficient data availability for rollups while keeping node operation accessible.

nodes.label: zkEVM
nodes.rationale: Zero-knowledge proofs could let validators verify Ethereum blocks without re-executing transactions, enabling higher gas limits without raising hardware requirements.

nodes.label: Real-Time Proving (RTP)
nodes.rationale: Race to mainnet-grade L1 zkEVMs staged in phases (performance sprint, security sprint, delayed proving, mandatory proving, enshrined proofs); RTP eligibility demands sub-10-second proofs, with a healthy cohort proving at least 70 percent of blocks in under 10s. Current cohort sits at 93.7 percent sub-10s across ~200k proofs.

nodes.rationale: A formal record of the details and supply-chain relationships of components used in building software, with minimum elements mandated to bring transparency to the software supply chain.

nodes.label: SLSA
nodes.rationale: Specification for describing and incrementally improving supply-chain security, established by industry consensus and organized into levels of increasing security guarantees.

nodes.label: Cairo
nodes.rationale: Created because hand-written constraints greatly limited feature velocity for StarkEx: a CPU Algebraic Intermediate Representation whose single AIR verifies the instruction set, opening proofs for arbitrary computational statements in a faster and safer manner.

nodes.label: SHARP (Shared Prover)
nodes.rationale: Takes transactions from several separate apps and proves them all in one STARK proof, filling proof capacity faster and improving rate and latency.

nodes.label: Applicative Recursion
nodes.rationale: Application-aware recursion merges both the proofs and their public inputs (state update A to B plus B to C becomes A to C) and compresses rollup data across multiple L2 blocks - independent of and combinable with application-agnostic recursion.

nodes.label: Layer 3 Deployments
nodes.rationale: Baking the Recursive Verifier statement into a StarkNet smart contract lets proofs be submitted to L2, enabling L3s whose proofs aggregate recursively down to a single proof verified on L2.

nodes.label: Recursive STARK Proving
nodes.rationale: A Cairo program that verifies other STARK proofs exploits logarithmic compression: verifying takes roughly log(T) of the T needed to prove, so proofs of proofs are cheap. Recursion removes the compute-resource ceiling on statement size, cuts on-chain verification cost per transaction by orders of magnitude, and reduces latency because statements are proven in parallel as they arrive - a rare case of scale and latency improving together.

nodes.label: Data Availability Sampling
nodes.rationale: If done with ZKPs or polynomial commitments, safe under asynchrony - the key safety argument for sharding data rather than execution.

nodes.label: Optimistic Rollups
nodes.rationale: The near-term workhorse because ZK rollups could not yet support general-purpose EVM computation; easily extensible to generic EVM applications unlike plasma, which suits only payments and DEX.

nodes.label: Rollup-Centric Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Base-layer scalability was years away while rollups were already live, so Ethereum retrenches to consensus and data availability (phase 1.5 and done). Sharding data availability is much safer than sharding EVM computation: fraud proofs need a strict two-epoch synchrony assumption while data availability sampling is safe under asynchrony. Also leaves economic space for L2 tokens to fund development the credibly-neutral base layer cannot.

nodes.label: ZK Rollups
nodes.rationale: Preferred once general-purpose EVM support arrives: short finality and exit times (minutes vs days), cheaper data, better security at large value locked, low-cost privacy, and self-verifying proof generation that decentralizes better than optimistic aggregation.

nodes.label: ZK Email Account Recovery

nodes.rationale: ZK Email component with circuit architecture, contract architecture, relayer infrastructure, and an extensions SDK for driving on-chain wallets from emails.

nodes.label: ZK Email

nodes.label: ZK-Regex
nodes.rationale: Regex matching inside zero-knowledge circuits, used by ZK Email to extract and prove properties of email content.

nodes.label: Halo2 Proving System
nodes.rationale: Selected by EZKL as its underlying cryptographic framework for its public auditing through years of previous development and overall completeness; EZKL is not limited to Halo2 and is incorporating additional systems.

nodes.label: Lilith Compute Cluster
nodes.rationale: Local proof generation limits very large models and rapid concurrent verification, so Lilith offloads proving to a remote high-performance cluster, mirroring the ezkl CLI and offering REST API access for concurrent, low-latency proof generation.

nodes.label: ONNX Model Format
nodes.rationale: Chosen as EZKL's circuit-compilation input format because it is widely used in the broader machine learning community, letting tree models, transformers, CNNs and RNNs be decomposed into circuit-representable operations.

nodes.label: Pessimistic Proofs
nodes.rationale: Security model for heterogeneous cross-chain interop: a compromised chain cannot drain more than its own deposits, so damage is contained mathematically rather than by trusting each connected chain.

nodes.label: DO-178C
nodes.rationale: RTCA standard 'Software Considerations in Airborne Systems and Equipment Certification' - the process-based assurance regime for avionics software.

nodes.label: HyperNova
nodes.rationale: Nova's zero-knowledge property is achieved by folding the IVC proof with a random instance prior to compression, an idea described in the HyperNova paper.

nodes.label: Mercury Commitment Scheme
nodes.rationale: Optimized variant providing faster verification than HyperKZG on pairing-friendly curves.

nodes.label: MicroSpartan
nodes.rationale: Preprocessing variant of Spartan ensuring the verifier's run time does not depend on the size of the step circuit.

nodes.label: Nova
nodes.rationale: Simplest recursive proof system in the literature yet fastest prover, with a constant-sized verifier circuit of about 10,000 multiplication gates. Maintainers deliberately prioritize code simplicity over minor performance gains to keep auditing for correctness and security tractable.

nodes.label: Powers of Tau Universal Setup
nodes.rationale: A single universal setup is reused across circuits and shared with other KZG-based systems; production deployments should use a ceremony like the Ethereum Perpetual Powers of Tau where only one honest participant is needed for security.

nodes.label: Veridise Nova Article Series
nodes.rationale: Stored capture returned a Medium 404 page; the node stands in for the cited accessible exposition of Nova and folding schemes.

nodes.label: Cycle of Elliptic Curves
nodes.rationale: For efficiency Nova is instantiated over a cycle of curves (Pallas/Vesta, BN254/Grumpkin, secp/secq); the instantiation has its own security proof (IACR ePrint 2023/969).

nodes.label: Folding Scheme
nodes.rationale: Reduces the task of checking two NP statements to checking a single NP statement - the simple primitive from which Nova's recursion is built.

nodes.label: Incrementally Verifiable Computation (IVC)
nodes.rationale: Prover updates proof pi_i to pi_i+1 with work independent of the number of steps executed so far, and verifier work does not grow with computation length. Enables rollups, VDFs, succinct blockchains, verifiable state machines, and proofs of (virtual) machine executions such as EVM and RISC-V.

nodes.label: C2PA Assertion
nodes.rationale: Statements covering asset creation, edit actions, capture device details, and content bindings; they are trust signals a human uses to assess trustworthiness, and can be redacted for privacy.

nodes.label: C2PA Manifest
nodes.rationale: Verifiable unit binding assertions, the claim, and the claim signature together via JUMBF; the set of manifests stored in an asset's Content Credential represents its provenance data and remains valid indefinitely.

nodes.label: C2PA Claim
nodes.rationale: Digitally signed entity wrapping assertions with additional information; signing produces the claim signature that anchors tamper-evidence.

nodes.label: C2PA Claim Generator
nodes.rationale: Hardware or software component (e.g. a C2PA-enabled camera) that binds assertions, claims, and the claim signature into a C2PA Manifest embedded in the asset.

nodes.label: C2PA Hard Binding
nodes.rationale: Cryptographic hashes that bind the manifest to the exact asset content, providing tamper-evidence.

nodes.label: C2PA Soft Binding
nodes.rationale: Content-derived (e.g. perceptual) binding that can survive transformations where a hard binding would break, allowing manifest recovery for modified assets.

nodes.label: ZKPassport
nodes.rationale: Privacy-preserving identity verification from passports, national IDs, and residence permits; proofs are generated on the user's own phone and reveal only the requested attributes and nothing else, minimizing personal data exposure. Offers self-served in-code queries or dashboard-managed policies for auditable, redeploy-free request changes.

nodes.label: Data Integrity and Enveloping Proofs (JOSE/COSE)
nodes.rationale: Two securing approaches for credentials: embedded Data Integrity proofs and enveloping signatures using JOSE/COSE, giving implementers a choice of securing mechanism.

nodes.label: Verifiable Credential
nodes.rationale: A specific way to express a set of claims made by an issuer, such as a driver's license or education certificate, in an extensible data model secured from tampering.

nodes.label: Verifiable Presentation
nodes.rationale: Holder-assembled package of one or more verifiable credentials (or data derived from them) presented to a verifier, including enveloped variants.

nodes.label: C2PA Technical Specification
nodes.rationale: Deliberately makes no value judgments about whether provenance data is good or bad, only whether assertions validate as associated with the asset, correctly formed, and tamper-free; follows Technology Minimalism by relying on prior well-established techniques and enables global opt-in adoption.

nodes.label: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0

nodes.label: C2PA Trust Model
nodes.rationale: Trust decisions are based on the identity of the signer of the claim; claim signatures combined with trusted time-stamps can be validated indefinitely to check that credentials were valid and unrevoked at signing time, using X.509 certificates and trust lists.

nodes.label: Proof of Personhood
nodes.rationale: Using zero-knowledge proofs over government identity documents to establish that a user is a unique real person, supporting KYC without full identity disclosure.

nodes.label: Selective Disclosure of Identity Attributes
nodes.rationale: Requesting and verifying specific identity attributes such as age or nationality (e.g. gte age 18) without exposing any unnecessary personal information.

nodes.label: Selective Disclosure (VC Data Model)
nodes.rationale: Privacy mechanism letting a holder reveal only a subset of the claims in a credential to a verifier.

nodes.label: Issuer-Holder-Verifier Ecosystem
nodes.rationale: Three-party exchange model composed of issuers, holders, and verifiers; the holder mediates presentation of credentials, which supports privacy by decoupling issuance from verification.

nodes.label: Data Availability
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: The only way the operator can cheat is by withholding data; users should not accept a transfer unless chain data is available, and a new operator should only join from a state for which they possess all data, or they risk being slashed by an unserviceable priority-queue request.

nodes.label: zk-Rollup (Roll_up Construction)
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: Operator aggregates off-chain user transactions into a single on-chain SNARK-verified state update over a Merkle tree, so gas per state transition is constant regardless of transaction count; scalability is bounded by economically provable SNARK size (~60k constraints/tx, ~17000 tps estimated) rather than gasBlockLimit/gasPerTx.

nodes.label: Airbender
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: RISC-V prover delivering subsecond block proofs and minutes-to-Ethereum settlement on commodity GPUs (~$0.0001/transfer); general-purpose — compiles EVM bytecode, WASM, or Rust without code changes — enabling latency-sensitive financial activity and real-time settlement.

nodes.label: Elastic Network (ZKsync Chains)
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: Network of interoperable public and private ZK Chains secured by cryptography rather than validators, with ~1s network hops, minutes-to-Ethereum finality, and atomic privacy-preserving cross-chain settlement (ZKsync Connect) that eliminates third-party bridges.

nodes.label: Prividium
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: Permissioned validium: private, Ethereum-secured L2 that keeps transaction data and state off-chain while posting only ZK validity proofs to Ethereum. Resolves the bank dilemma of control vs. connectivity — private execution with public verifiability, selective regulator disclosure, and no trusted operator required.

nodes.label: Tokenized Deposits
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: Programmable, always-on digital money issued by regulated banks and anchored to Ethereum, combining blockchain programmability with deposit insurance and the regulatory framework of traditional banking; Cari Network is onboarding U.S. regional banks with $600B+ in deposits onto Prividium.

nodes.label: ZK Stack
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: Open-source framework for building customizable, enterprise-grade ZK blockchains that scale globally, interoperate natively, and inherit Ethereum's security; enterprises choose chain type (rollup/validium), data availability, gas token, sequencing, and permissioned vs. permissionless access.

nodes.label: Operator Auction
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: After slashing, a replacement operator is chosen by auction: bidders post a deposit and the state they wish to resume from; the highest bid on the most recent sidechain state wins. Operators need only be rational, not honest — bidding on newer states is advantageous, and a minimum stake deters repeat misbehavior.

nodes.label: Priority Queue Exit
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: Users request withdrawals at the smart-contract level; if the operator fails to serve the queue within a time limit, data is assumed unavailable and the operator is slashed. This forces the worst case (malicious operator) to degrade to an on-chain token where funds cannot be stolen or withheld for meaningful time.

nodes.label: Roll Back Mechanism
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: If data becomes unavailable the operator is replaced and the chain rolls back to a previously valid state, exiting users on request along the way; because SNARKs disallow invalid state transitions, recovery from a malicious operator does not force all users to exit, unlike Plasma's competitive mass-exit withdrawals. Leaves already exited can never exit again, preventing double withdrawal across rollbacks.

nodes.label: SNARK-Verified State Transition
nodes.community_name: Ref 136 Roll Up Roll Back Snark Side Cha
nodes.rationale: The operator proves that (previous state + set of transactions) produces the new state; the proof is verified inside the EVM and the Merkle root updated only if valid. The SNARK compresses signatures — explicit signatures need not be posted because the proof is implicit evidence they exist.

nodes.label: Composable Proofs
nodes.rationale: Mina's zero-knowledge proofs are modular: prove anything in one application and reuse it in another, across app-chains, roll-ups, zkVMs, and L2s.

nodes.label: zkApps (Zero-Knowledge Applications)
nodes.rationale: Turing-complete TypeScript-based smart contracts with programmable privacy: user data never leaves the local device, only proofs are submitted to the chain, extending beyond the conventional definition of a smart contract.

nodes.label: Mina Protocol
nodes.rationale: Positions itself as the ZK blockchain for a secure, private and verifiable internet: succinctness lowers the barrier to participation, which the project argues yields robust security and unrivaled decentralization with minimal resource requirements.

nodes.label: Coda Protocol
nodes.rationale: The captured page shows codaprotocol.com is now a parked/for-sale domain; the original project content is no longer served there.

nodes.label: Constant-Size Succinct Blockchain (22KB)
nodes.rationale: A fixed 22KB chain (versus hundreds of GB and growing for other blockchains) keeps resource requirements minimal, lowering the barrier to participation and enabling decentralization.

nodes.label: Off-Chain Computation with On-Chain Proof Verification
nodes.norm_label: off-chain computation with on-chain proof verification
nodes.rationale: Run computation off-chain and verify a single proof representing infinite computation on-chain, reducing strain on the network, lowering fees and enhancing scalability.

nodes.label: Proof of Everything (Recursive ZK Proof)
nodes.rationale: All chain history is rolled up into one singular, recursive, constant-sized proof so any device can join and verify the entire Mina chain in milliseconds while retaining full node security.

nodes.label: gadgetlib1
nodes.rationale: Low-level template-based gadget library exposing all ppzkSNARK features and supporting multiple elliptic curves simultaneously; used for most internal constraint building including reductions and PCD.

nodes.label: gadgetlib2
nodes.rationale: Alternative gadget library chosen to be better documented and easier to use with a template-free interface, at the cost of providing fewer useful gadgets than gadgetlib1.

nodes.label: Groth16 Proof System
nodes.rationale: R1CS zk-SNARK secure in the generic group model; faster with shorter proofs than BCTV14a at the expense of stronger security assumptions.

nodes.label: Preprocessing zkSNARK (ppzkSNARK)
nodes.rationale: Requires a circuit-specific generator run once to produce a long proving key and short verification key before any proofs can be created or verified; follows and optimizes BCTV14a, itself building on BCGTV13, GGPR13, and BCIOP13.

nodes.label: Proof-Carrying Data (PCD)
nodes.rationale: Implemented via recursive composition of SNARKs as explained in BCCT13 and optimized in BCTV14b using cycles of elliptic curves; enables scalable TinyRAM proving and zero-knowledge cluster MapReduce (CTV15).

nodes.label: Rank-1 Constraint System (R1CS)
nodes.rationale: NP-complete language of equations <A,(1,X)>*<B,(1,X)>=<C,(1,X)> over a prime field; arithmetic and boolean circuits reduce to it gate-by-gate, making it the common target language for SNARK frontends.

nodes.label: TinyRAM
nodes.rationale: Random access machine whose code execution (obtainable by compiling from C) is proven with libsnark's proof systems per BCTV14a/BCGTV13; adaptable to any RAM with a simple load-store interface.

nodes.label: zkSNARK
nodes.rationale: Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-interactive ARgument of Knowledge: zero knowledge, succinctness, non-interactivity, computational soundness, and proof of knowledge; also described as succinct non-interactive computationally-sound zero-knowledge proofs of knowledge.

nodes.label: libsnark zkSNARK Library
nodes.rationale: Research-quality C++ zkSNARK library by SCIPR Lab; explicitly not production-ready, with known timing/cache side channels and /dev/urandom randomness caveats.

nodes.label: Recursive Composition of SNARKs
nodes.rationale: Verifying one SNARK inside another so proofs can attest to arbitrarily long or distributed computations; the mechanism underlying PCD and bootstrapping (BCCT13, BCTV14b).

nodes.label: Structural AST Extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free — structural extraction of code avoids LLM token cost entirely.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit with no background process, works with any editor; appends to an existing hook rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Avoids re-paying LLM token cost for files already extracted in prior runs.

nodes.label: Graphify Skill
nodes.rationale: Built around the Karpathy /raw workflow: persistent graph survives sessions, an honest audit trail distinguishes found vs invented edges, and community detection surfaces cross-document connections the user would never think to ask about.

nodes.label: Incremental Update (--update)
nodes.rationale: Only re-extracts new/changed files to save tokens and time.

nodes.label: Query Result Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Answers are saved to graphify-out/memory so the next --update extracts each Q&A as a graph node, improving future queries.

nodes.label: Karpathy /raw Folder Workflow
nodes.rationale: Drop anything into one folder — papers, tweets, screenshots, code, notes — and let structure emerge from extraction rather than manual organization.

nodes.label: Parallel Semantic Extraction Subagents
nodes.rationale: Subagent dispatch in a single message is mandated because sequential one-by-one file reading is 5-10x slower.

nodes.label: URL Ingestion (/graphify add)
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects source type (Twitter/X oEmbed, arXiv, PDF, image, webpage) and saves into ./raw with author/contributor attribution before an incremental graph update.

nodes.label: Watch Mode Auto-Rebuild
nodes.rationale: Code-only changes rebuild via AST with no LLM; doc/image changes only flag needs_update because semantic re-extraction costs tokens. Debounce prevents one rebuild per file during agent write waves.

nodes.label: Wiki Frontmatter Schema
nodes.rationale: created/updated are explicit ISO dates because git resets filesystem mtime on checkout — file.ctime cannot be trusted.

nodes.label: Five Wiki Page Types
nodes.rationale: Concepts are atomic (one idea per page — splitting is correct, merging usually wrong), sources and syntheses are deliberately aggregate, entities map one-per-proper-noun; this keeps cross-reference links precise.

nodes.label: ZES Evidence Tiers
nodes.rationale: Optional 0-3 strength annotations for fine-grained epistemic tracking; the core status field remains mandatory.

nodes.label: Marp Slides (Optional)
nodes.rationale: Wikilinks and embeds do not render in Marp, so marp: true is banned on standard page templates and decks live in a separate slides/ directory outside wiki content.

nodes.label: Obsidian Setup
nodes.rationale: Workspace noise is gitignored but app.json/hotkeys/plugin config stay tracked so Obsidian behavior travels with the repo across machines; attachments live in raw/assets/ co-located with immutable sources.

nodes.label: Batch Ingest
nodes.rationale: Opt-in only; per-source confirmation, fresh dedup, and one atomic commit per source are preserved even in a batch.

nodes.label: Ingest Operation
nodes.rationale: The primary knowledge-accretion loop: source read in full before any claim is written (anti-hallucination guarantee), takeaways discussed with the user before writing, and index updates never deferred because index staleness is the top operational risk.

nodes.label: Init Operation
nodes.rationale: Creates structure only — no stub pages, no faux overview thesis, no speculative maps — because fabricating content with no raw/ source to cite violates provenance; git init plus first commit is mandatory as the baseline safety layer.

nodes.label: Lint Fix Loop
nodes.rationale: Prioritized: structural blockers first, then navigation correctness, discoverability, provenance integrity, and only then semantic accuracy (flag-only) and enrichment.

nodes.label: lint.py Mechanical Accelerator
nodes.rationale: Stdlib-only checker for broken links, orphans, missing frontmatter, and unsourced claims; navigation scaffolding files are exempt because they are catalogs, not content pages.

nodes.label: Query Operation
nodes.rationale: Every claim either carries a wikilink citation to a page read this session, is labeled as non-wiki knowledge, or triggers abstention — there is no third option.

nodes.label: Synthesis File-Back
nodes.rationale: A well-evidenced answer is preserved as a first-class synthesis page with a two-level citation chain (synthesis -> concept/entity page -> raw source) and a 'Derived page' marker; it is an ingest-grade write with full commit discipline.

nodes.label: Two-Level Scrape Dedup
nodes.rationale: URL normalization (scheme/www/tracking-param variants share one dedup key) plus content-hash comparison makes re-fetching idempotent — mirrors and variants produce reported skips, not duplicate raw files.

nodes.label: Fetcher Tier Escalation (http/stealth/dynamic)
nodes.rationale: Escalation is narrow and signal-based (HTTP 401/403/429, challenge markers, near-zero extracted text) — not fuzzy guessing; dynamic is the terminal tier and the tier used is recorded in frontmatter.

nodes.label: Scrape/Crawl Operation
nodes.rationale: An optional Claude-Code-only on-ramp: it only prepares raw/ files; the wiki itself is always written by the standard v1 ingest. Crawls always plan first (--plan-only) as a runaway and cost control.

nodes.label: WebFetch Fallback
nodes.rationale: Last-resort single-URL capture when Scrapling is declined or unavailable; output is model-interpreted, so it is stamped is_verbatim: false and may never be quoted verbatim.

nodes.label: llm-wiki Eval Suite
nodes.rationale: Checks that the skill triggers when it should, stays quiet when it shouldn't (negative cases like third-party wikis and ad-hoc notes), and that each operation behaves correctly; re-run after editing descriptions or playbooks.

nodes.label: Edge Confidence Audit Trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS)
nodes.rationale: Every edge is tagged so the user knows what was found versus invented; uncertainty is flagged AMBIGUOUS rather than omitted.

nodes.label: Graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge; always show token cost and raw cohesion scores; warn before oversized HTML viz — the graph's value depends on trustworthiness.

nodes.label: Append-Never-Overwrite Contradiction Rule
nodes.rationale: When sources disagree, both positions go in a [!conflict] callout with status: contested; deciding which claim is canonical is a human decision, never Claude's. Supersession (newer authoritative value) is distinct and keeps a dated note of the old value.

nodes.label: Dedup Before Create
nodes.rationale: Three-step search (index.md, category _index.md, aliases) plus filename-equals-canonical-title makes re-ingest idempotent and prevents duplicate pages.

nodes.label: Index Router and MOC Discipline
nodes.rationale: index.md is a router, not a full listing — keeping per-query token cost roughly flat as the wiki grows; MOCs split at ~25-30 entries so any navigational file stays scannable in one pass. Links express aboutness; tags express context/state.

nodes.label: Orphan Prevention Rule
nodes.rationale: Every new page needs one outbound wikilink, one MOC entry, and one category index entry before commit so it stays discoverable in the graph.

nodes.label: Inline Provenance Marker
nodes.rationale: A bare source link without a locator is insufficient (UNSOURCED lint defect); quote anchors written only from the open raw file prevent hallucination drift from prior model memory.

nodes.label: Wikilink-Only Internal Linking
nodes.rationale: Markdown links break Obsidian backlinks, graph view, and Dataview queries; standardizing on [[wikilinks]] keeps all three working. Renames must go through Obsidian or update all referrers in the same commit.

nodes.label: Atomic Ingest Commit
nodes.rationale: One commit per ingest is the unit of undo (git revert), the backup mechanism, and the provenance audit trail; partial state breaks the invariants lint and query depend on. The raw source is committed too so citations are reproducible from the repo alone.

nodes.label: Wiki Discovery Contract
nodes.rationale: A directory is a wiki iff CLAUDE.md's first non-empty line is the '<!-- llm-wiki: v1 -->' marker AND a wiki/ folder exists; walking up from cwd makes every operation auto-discover the wiki without configuration — nothing is hardcoded to a specific repo.

nodes.label: Canonical Prose Semantic Pass
nodes.rationale: The LLM's prose pass is the canonical lint so linting works fully on surfaces without code execution; the script only accelerates the stable mechanical subset and cannot drift from prose conventions.

nodes.label: Query Abstention Behavior
nodes.rationale: 'I don't have enough in the wiki to answer that' is a correct, complete answer — always preferable to a confident answer drawn from model memory; the abstention suggests a concrete source to ingest.

nodes.label: Index-First Read Path
nodes.rationale: Three-level drill-down (root index, category index, page) keeps token cost roughly flat as the wiki grows and guards against answering from a stale or guessed page name.

nodes.label: Parametric Knowledge Labeling
nodes.rationale: Model-memory content must be labeled adjacent and unambiguously ('not from wiki') so the user always knows which parts of an answer are wiki-grounded; the label is not a license to pad answers with model memory.

nodes.label: is_verbatim Provenance Flag
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes byte-derived extraction (quotable verbatim) from model-interpreted WebFetch content (paraphrase only) — preserving the wiki's exact-quote provenance integrity.

nodes.label: Scrape Surface Gate
nodes.rationale: Fetch attempts on the API sandbox or claude.ai fail or hang (no network, no installs), so the gate forces a clean refusal with fallback options instead of retries or browser downloads.

nodes.rationale: Generalizes the FRI IOPP so it works over any foldable linear code in linear time, removing FRI's dependence on FFT-friendly Reed-Solomon fields; equivalent to FRI when instantiated with Reed-Solomon codes.

nodes.label: BaseFold Multilinear Polynomial Commitment Scheme
nodes.rationale: Interleaves the BaseFold IOPP with the classical sumcheck protocol under shared verifier randomness so the IOPP's final oracle answers the sumcheck's last query, yielding a field-agnostic multilinear PCS; field-agnosticism avoids encoding mod-p operations in-circuit (ECDSA drops from 2^20 to 2^14 constraints).

nodes.rationale: Predefined operations implemented directly as equation sets rather than Cairo code, chosen to erase the performance overhead of moving from hand-written AIRs to CPU-executed programs.

nodes.label: Foldable Linear Code
nodes.rationale: A linear code whose generator matrix decomposes recursively via diagonal matrices, generalizing the structure of Reed-Solomon codes exploited by FRI.

nodes.label: Holographic Proof
nodes.rationale: The verifier queries an encoding of the circuit rather than reading it, which yields preprocessing SNARGs in the random oracle model and enables post-quantum, transparent recursive composition without special algebraic objects.

nodes.label: Nondeterministic Continuous Read-Only Memory
nodes.rationale: Prover-chosen immutable memory model adopted because its restrictions yield a very efficient AIR: only 5 trace cells per memory access, critical since each instruction performs 4 accesses.

nodes.label: Random Foldable Codes (RFC)
nodes.rationale: A special type of punctured Reed-Muller codes with uniformly random diagonal folding matrices Ti and Ti' = -Ti; foldable and efficiently encodable over any sufficiently large field, with proven tight minimum-distance bounds.

nodes.label: FRI Blowup Factor
nodes.rationale: A larger blowup factor slows the prover (more evaluations to Merkle-hash) but shrinks verification cost and proof length; the parameter is a deliberate prover-time versus verifier-cost trade-off.

nodes.rationale: A bad actor can store a ledger replica today and decrypt it once a sufficiently powerful quantum computer exists, so PQC upgrades cannot retroactively protect the privacy of previously recorded transactions.

nodes.label: Hedged Signing

nodes.label: HyperPlonk
nodes.rationale: Replaces the subgroup Omega with the Boolean hypercube and T with a multilinear polynomial, turning quasilinear ZeroTests into linear-time operations for a linear-time prover.

nodes.label: Plonk polynomial IOP
nodes.rationale: Encodes the computation trace as one polynomial T over a multiplicative subgroup and verifies four things: correct public inputs (ZeroTest vs v(X)), correct gates (selector polynomial S), correct wiring (T invariant under rotation permutation W), and zero output; abstract IOP combinable with any PCS - KZG gives Aztec/JellyFish, Bulletproofs gives Halo2, FRI gives Plonky2.

nodes.label: Plookup (lookup arguments in Plonkish tables)
nodes.rationale: Verifying membership of table values in predefined lists shrinks trace rows and thus prover time.

nodes.label: Prescribed permutation check (bivariate pair encoding)
nodes.rationale: Direct ZeroTest on f(y)-g(W(y)) would compose degrees to k^2 and force a quadratic prover; encoding (W(a),f(a)) vs (a,g(a)) pairs as bivariate root polynomials reduces it to a linear-time ProductCheck.

nodes.label: ZeroTest on a set Omega (quotient by vanishing polynomial)
nodes.norm_label: zerotest on a set omega (quotient by vanishing polynomial)
nodes.rationale: f is zero on Omega iff Z_Omega divides f; the prover can only KZG-commit to the quotient if it is a genuine polynomial, which is what proves divisibility.

nodes.label: FRI Low Degree Test

nodes.rationale: Concepts ranked by centrality and reference support, each tagged well-covered / under-covered / absent versus the manuscript with a per-chapter rollup - the graph's recommendation engine for the book.

nodes.label: Two-Phase Extraction Strategy
nodes.rationale: Parallel mechanical extraction first, then an enrichment pass with global visibility - extraction is embarrassingly parallel but enrichment needs cross-chapter context (entity map, dependencies, contradictions).

nodes.label: Book Graph (book-graph/)
nodes.rationale: An independent manuscript-only graph in its own directory never touches graph 1, preserving a clean comparison baseline.

nodes.label: Reference Subgraph Augmentation
nodes.rationale: Reuses graph 1's already-mined reference nodes instead of re-extracting; scrapling re-runs only as an idempotent confirmation of the corpus.

nodes.label: Vocabulary Drift Risk
nodes.rationale: Different concept ids for the same idea would understate overlap; subagents prefer graph 1's existing concept ids and the comparison matches on normalized labels.

nodes.label: Shared concept_<kebab> Node IDs
nodes.rationale: Shared concept ids are how distinct papers interlink on merge - the source of cross-paper surprising connections; imprecise names risk wrongly merging distinct concepts.

nodes.label: Subagent Extraction Contract
nodes.rationale: Fixed prompt: read the full PDF, emit 10-25 nodes (constructions, theorems, assumptions, citations), every node anchored, source_location required, uncertain edges tagged AMBIGUOUS - caps over-generation.

nodes.label: Master Graph (master-graph/)
nodes.rationale: A new directory unifies the three graphs while leaving them untouched as provenance and comparison baselines (augmenting graphify-out in place was rejected).

nodes.label: Per-Chapter Split Extraction
nodes.rationale: A single-file extraction of the 919 KB manuscript extracts shallowly (the same failure dense PDFs showed), so the book is split at chapter headings with one extraction subagent per chapter.

nodes.label: Additive Anchored Extraction
nodes.rationale: Additive so existing chapter-to-paper cross-edges survive; anchored to each paper's existing node ids so new deep nodes attach to the right place in the graph.

nodes.label: Brakedown
nodes.rationale: Built the PCS from tensor-query IOPs and proved knowledge soundness without an efficient decoding algorithm, freeing the code design space.

nodes.label: Code-based polynomial commitment (Ligero/Brakedown style)
nodes.rationale: Coefficients arranged as a sqrt(d) x sqrt(d) matrix, rows encoded with a linear code, columns Merkle-committed; transparent constant-size setup, plausibly post-quantum, field-agnostic, linear-time hash-and-field prover; tradeoff: sqrt(d) proofs of megabytes in practice.

nodes.label: Linear code
nodes.rationale: Any linear combination of codewords is a codeword; encoding is a vector-matrix product with the generator matrix, and minimum distance equals minimum weight of a nonzero codeword.

nodes.label: Lossless expander (near-maximal bipartite expansion)
nodes.rationale: Small subsets expand to (1-beta)*g*|S| neighbors; unique-neighbor counting turns small-weight messages into non-zero encodings, which is what gives the recursive Spielman construction constant relative distance.

nodes.label: Orion
nodes.rationale: Code-switching proof composition cuts proof size to O(log^2 d) (~50MB to 5.7MB) and adds an expander-testing algorithm, via graph density, that makes randomly sampled lossless expanders reliable.

nodes.label: Proximity test (random row combination vs opened columns)
nodes.norm_label: proximity test (random row combination vs opened columns)
nodes.rationale: Guarantees the committed matrix is close to a genuinely encoded matrix regardless of the evaluation point; needed because the consistency check alone uses a structured, non-random vector the prover could anticipate.

nodes.label: Reed-Solomon code
nodes.rationale: Message viewed as a degree k-1 polynomial evaluated at n public points; distance n-k+1 (optimal), rate and relative distance both constant at n=2k; O(n log n) encoding via FFT.

nodes.label: Spielman linear-time encodable code (1996; Druk-Ishai 2014)
nodes.rationale: Recursive systematic construction: copy message, expand, recursively encode, expand again; constant rate 1/4 and constant relative distance with strictly linear-time encoding.

nodes.label: Lattice Bulletproofs Folding Technique
nodes.rationale: Adapts the Bulletproofs recursive folding to Ring-SIS commitments; monomial challenge sets are used because 2/(X^i-X^j) has {-1,0,1} coefficients, which bounds coefficient growth of extracted solutions at each fold.

nodes.label: Arithmetic Secret-Sharing Linearization over Number Rings
nodes.norm_label: arithmetic secret-sharing linearization over number rings
nodes.rationale: Shamir evaluation points must come from exceptional subsets with invertible differences; small rings are handled by moving the secret sharing to a ring extension while preventing dishonest provers from using extension elements.

nodes.label: Compressed Sigma-Protocols (Lattice Instantiation)
nodes.rationale: Basic sigma-protocols for opening linear forms on committed vectors are compressed with a Bulletproofs-style folding, then circuit ZK is reduced to the linear case via arithmetic secret sharing adapted from MPC.

nodes.label: Tight Knowledge Extraction for (k1,...,kmu)-Special Soundness

nodes.label: Baloo Lookup Argument
nodes.rationale: Reduces the lookup relation to proving existence of a secret lookup matrix M with M*t = a, importing Marlin-style Checkable Subspace Sampling; deliberately keeps homomorphic table commitments (which Flookup gives up) to support commit-and-prove expansions and multi-column tables for zkEVM use, at the cost of slightly higher constants.

nodes.label: cq Lookup Argument (Cached Quotients)
nodes.rationale: Caches per-Lagrange-basis quotient commitments in an O(N log N) preprocessing step so the prover can run the logarithmic-derivative lookup directly on the original large table, avoiding subtable extraction on arbitrary point sets (the O(n log^2 n) bottleneck of Flookup and Baloo); keeping all prover-defined pairing arguments in G1 makes proofs conveniently aggregatable and table commitments stay homomorphic for vector lookups.

nodes.label: Flookup Protocol
nodes.rationale: First lookup with prover time quasi-linear in the number of lookups and independent of table size, via fractional decomposition; trade-offs: table commitments are non-homomorphic (roots of a vanishing polynomial) and verification needs a pairing with a prover-defined G2 point, hurting recursive aggregation and vector lookups.

nodes.label: Fractional Sumcheck

nodes.label: Lookup Argument

nodes.label: Zero-knowledge property

nodes.label: Interactive oracle proof (IOP)

nodes.label: Polynomial commitment scheme

nodes.label: Merkle tree (vector commitment)

nodes.label: Bulletproofs polynomial commitment (transparent halving reduction)

nodes.rationale: Additivity of the commitment space alone (not succinct or efficient Eval) suffices for efficient aggregation, and hence PCD/IVC can be built from any homomorphic PCS, generalizing the Halo methodology.

nodes.label: Almost Special Soundness (ASS)
nodes.rationale: Introduced to close the gap in DARK's original security proof: DARK is not special-sound, but its structure lets a bounded-norm extraction predicate replace special soundness while preserving knowledge soundness.

nodes.label: DARK Polynomial Commitment Scheme
nodes.rationale: Uses Diophantine Arguments of Knowledge over integer encodings of polynomials in groups of unknown order; instantiated with class groups it removes the trusted setup entirely, making the compiled SNARK transparent.

nodes.label: Lattice Bulletproofs Folding
nodes.rationale: Adapts the Bulletproofs halving/folding technique to Ring-SIS commitments using monomial challenge spaces to bound extracted-witness growth per fold; achieves polylogarithmic proofs at the cost of large slack.

nodes.label: Sumcheck Argument
nodes.rationale: Recasts Pedersen-style folding techniques as instances of the sumcheck protocol over modules, so disparate cryptographic settings (discrete log, pairings, unknown-order groups, lattices) share one framework, one extractor, and answer open questions such as lattice-based succinct arguments from SIS.

nodes.label: Proof of Replication
nodes.rationale: Decodable VDFs give transparent proofs that a server stores a unique slow encoding of a (possibly public) file, replacing designated-verifier RSA time-lock constructions.

nodes.label: Randomness Beacon
nodes.rationale: Ideal service (Rabin) publishing unpredictable random values. VDFs are added after entropy extraction so a last-moving adversary (high-frequency trader, miner withholding blocks, last commit-reveal participant) cannot simulate outcomes fast enough to bias the beacon.

nodes.label: Sloth / Unicorn (Lenstra-Wesolowski)
nodes.rationale: Chained modular square-root puzzles giving a time-asymmetric encoding; characterized by the VDF paper as a pseudo-VDF because verification is not polylog(t).

nodes.label: Time-Lock Puzzle (Rivest-Shamir-Wagner)
nodes.rationale: Repeated squaring in an RSA group is inherently sequential, but unlike a VDF the verifier needs secret state to prepare and check each puzzle, so time-lock puzzles are not universally verifiable.

nodes.label: Verifiable Delay Function (VDF)
nodes.rationale: Setup/Eval/Verify triple: requires t sequential steps to evaluate even with polynomial parallelism, yet produces a unique output verifiable in polylog(t) time. Designed so no adversary can distinguish the output from random in less than a specified wall-clock time.

nodes.label: Boneh-Bonneau-Bünz-Fisch, Verifiable Delay Functions (CRYPTO 2018)
nodes.rationale: Formalizes verifiable delay functions and gives the first candidate constructions achieving an exponential gap between sequential evaluation time and public verification time; motivated by manipulation-resistant randomness beacons and resource-efficient blockchains.

nodes.label: Distributed FFT
nodes.rationale: FFTs over billion-degree polynomials exceed single-machine memory, so DIZK distributes them (with Lagrange interpolation and MSM) across a compute cluster to reach billion-gate circuits, 100x larger and 100x faster per gate than monolithic provers.

nodes.label: Energy-Saving Circuits
nodes.rationale: Standard QAP compilation makes the prover pay cryptographic effort for both sides of every branch; energy-saving circuits charge the prover only for the execution path actually taken, aligning cost with actual rather than worst-case execution time.

nodes.label: Groth16 3-Element SNARK
nodes.rationale: Compiles each LIP field element into a single group element and argues soundness in the generic group model instead of a falsifiable assumption, trading assumption strength for minimal proof size: 3 group elements verified with a single pairing product equation. Small proofs are prioritized because recursive SNARK composition makes proof size and verification cost compound.

nodes.label: Multi-Party Trusted Setup Ceremony
nodes.rationale: Whoever runs a zk-SNARK setup holds trapdoor information enabling fraudulent proofs (in Zcash, undetectable counterfeiting); generating the CRS with a multi-party round-robin protocol ensures no one can forge proofs unless every participant colludes, and statistical zero-knowledge holds even if all are malicious.

nodes.label: MultiQAP
nodes.rationale: Compiling C to a single QAP unrolls loops and inlines functions, blowing up circuit size; MultiQAPs connect smaller sub-QAPs with commitment buses that share state, shrinking keys and prover cost by up to two orders of magnitude while the bus raises QAP degree by only 1 versus tens or hundreds for Merkle-tree approaches.

nodes.label: Trusted Setup
nodes.rationale: zkSNARK setup uses secret randomness to sample public parameters; whoever holds the trapdoor can forge proofs, so the setup must be run by a trusted party or its risk mitigated via MPC ceremonies or updatable SRS.

nodes.label: Updatable Structured Reference String

nodes.label: Helped Batch Verification

nodes.label: Selective Verification

nodes.label: Universal Circuit

nodes.label: Progression-Free Sets
nodes.rationale: Elkin's progression-free set construction collapses the quadratic number of monomials in Groth's basic arguments to quasilinear, cutting CRS length and prover computation from quadratic to n^(1+o(1)).

nodes.label: Universal and Updatable SRS
nodes.rationale: Circuit-specific SRS forces a new cryptographic ceremony for every circuit change, which is unsustainable; a universal SRS supports all circuits up to a size bound and updatability means only one honest setup participant is needed for soundness.

nodes.label: FLI (Folding Lookup Instances)

nodes.label: Nebula

nodes.label: Multi-Instance k-Folding
nodes.rationale: Folds k instances in one operation using the Lagrange basis instead of Protostar's monomial basis, so degrees do not grow exponentially in k; the marginal verifier work per instance becomes constant field operations plus a logarithmic number of hashes, widening the tradeoff space between folding and decider costs.

nodes.label: Scribe

nodes.label: Ajtai Commitment Scheme
nodes.rationale: Additively homomorphic lattice commitment cm = Ax; binding only for low-norm vectors, so folding protocols must control witness norm growth.

nodes.label: Customizable Constraint System (CCS)
nodes.rationale: CCS simultaneously generalizes Plonkish, R1CS, and AIR without overheads, letting one folding scheme serve all major arithmetization formats.

nodes.label: CycleFold
nodes.rationale: General technique for instantiating folding-scheme-based recursive arguments over a 2-cycle of elliptic curves, avoiding a full folding verifier circuit on both curves.

nodes.label: CycleFold
nodes.rationale: Delegates only the folding verifier's few scalar multiplications to a tiny (~1,000-1,500 gate) circuit on the second curve instead of duplicating the whole verifier on both curves as in BCTV14/Nova, cutting the second-curve circuit nearly 10x and keeping the IVC construction and its security proof free of explicit cycle-of-curves reasoning.

nodes.label: Folding Scheme
nodes.rationale: Reduces checking two NP instances with the same structure to checking one, which suffices to build IVC while being simpler and far more efficient than a SNARK.

nodes.label: High-Arity Folding
nodes.rationale: Folding a large number of NP statements in a single shot avoids deep folding trees and removes Fiat-Shamir hash circuits from recursive statements, addressing both the heuristic security of instantiated random oracles and the dominant hashing cost in lattice-based folding verifiers.

nodes.label: Matrix Commitment Scheme
nodes.rationale: Neo commits to a vector over a small prime field by transforming it into a matrix and committing to that matrix, preserving the linear homomorphism needed for folding.

nodes.label: Multi-Folding Scheme
nodes.rationale: Folds multiple instances at once with prover cost of a single MSM, making generalizations of IVC such as PCD easier to build.

nodes.label: NovaBlindFold
nodes.rationale: Uses the blinding property of Nova's folding scheme to randomize IVC proofs, achieving zero-knowledge for free without zkSNARKs whose verifiers need expensive public-key operations.

nodes.label: Pay-per-Bit Commitment
nodes.rationale: Commitment costs scale with the bit-width of committed scalars (committing to bits is 32x cheaper than 32-bit values), removing LatticeFold's packing overheads and enabling small prime fields like Goldilocks.

nodes.label: Protogalaxy
nodes.rationale: Moves Protostar-style folding from the monomial to the Lagrange basis so k instances can be folded at once without exponentially growing degrees, and converts the accumulator to the new challenge instead of committing to a power vector; the marginal verifier work per instance becomes constant field operations for constant-degree gates.

nodes.label: Special-Sound Protocol
nodes.rationale: Starting from a simple special-sound protocol with an algebraic verifier gives a generic recipe: commit to prover messages, apply Fiat-Shamir, then accumulate the NARK verifier.

nodes.label: Tensor Reduction of Knowledge
nodes.rationale: Generalizes the central recursive step of split-and-fold arguments: for modules U = U1 (x) U2, evaluating a homomorphism in U reduces to evaluations in U1 and U2, explaining why sumcheck and inner-product arguments look different but feel the same.

nodes.label: Low-Norm Witness Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Writing witness entries in base b before folding, plus a sumcheck-based range proof, keeps extracted witnesses low-norm across unlimited folding rounds so Ajtai commitments stay binding.

nodes.label: DelegatedSpartan
nodes.rationale: Variant of Spartan for the non-pairing-friendly curve instance: the verifier exploits the repetitive circuit structure to evaluate R1CS matrix MLEs itself and delegates the polynomial evaluation to the prover via MicroSpartan, avoiding infeasible on-chain MSMs over Grumpkin.

nodes.label: Half-Pairing Curve Cycle (BN254/Grumpkin)
nodes.rationale: Chosen so the on-chain verifier can use Ethereum's BN254 precompiles and KZG commitments, while a CycleFold-style strategy shrinks the circuit on the non-pairing-friendly curve to ~1,300 gates.

nodes.label: HyperKZG
nodes.rationale: Modifies Gemini's reduction so multilinear polynomial evaluations in evaluation form reduce directly to batched univariate KZG openings without FFTs or interpolation.

nodes.label: MicroNova
nodes.rationale: Optimizes Nova's proof compression layer so compressed IVC proofs are O(log N) group elements verifiable with O(log N) scalar multiplications plus two pairings, enabling ~2.2M-gas Ethereum verification; uses KZG so any existing universal trusted setup can be reused.

nodes.label: MicroSpartan
nodes.rationale: Redesigns Spartan to minimize verifier cost: a single sum-check invocation reduces circuit satisfiability to one folded multilinear evaluation instance, at the cost of extra prover commitments tolerated because compression runs once after many IVC steps.

nodes.label: Code Switching (Proof Composition)

nodes.label: Computation Commitments

nodes.label: Modular Johnson-Lindenstrauss Norm Projection
nodes.rationale: Direct l2-norm checks on extracted witnesses are hard in lattice proofs; random modular JL projections preserve the l2 norm up to a factor of about 2.07, and proving the projection correct comes for free as additional dot-product constraints.

nodes.label: Linear-Time Prover
nodes.rationale: An O(N)-field-operation prover is regarded as the prerequisite for scaling SNARKs to large statements; FFTs and multiexponentiations are ruled out as superlinear, while Merkle hashing with suitable hash functions is counted as linear-time.

nodes.label: Merkle-Tree Paradigm (Kilian)
nodes.rationale: Merkle-tree succinct arguments rely only on generic hash functions and are quantum-safe, but their generic primitives inflate concrete proof sizes, which motivates lattice-based homomorphic alternatives.

nodes.label: Recursive Proof Composition
nodes.rationale: LaBRADOR recursively amortizes because proof size becomes dominated by the constant-size last recursion step, so proofs are nearly constant (47-58KB) across practical R1CS sizes; each iteration shrinks the witness from |s| to O(|s|^(2/3)), so only O(log log n) iterations are needed.

nodes.label: Computation Commitments
nodes.rationale: Sub-linear verification seems impossible because the verifier must process the NP statement; a one-time public preprocessing commits to sparse multilinear polynomials encoding the R1CS structure so later polynomial evaluations can be verifiably delegated to the prover, amortizing like GGPR's setup but without secret trapdoors, which is what makes Spartan transparent.

nodes.label: SPARK Sparse Polynomial Commitment Compiler
nodes.rationale: Transforms any extractable polynomial commitment scheme for multilinear polynomials into one that efficiently handles sparse multilinear polynomials using offline memory-checking circuits; the key to Spartan's time-optimal prover.

nodes.label: Split-and-Fold Technique
nodes.rationale: Split-and-fold arguments exploit the algebraic structure of homomorphic commitments to obtain proofs concretely smaller than Merkle-tree constructions; porting them to lattices is motivated by the analogous win of lattice signatures over hash-based ones.

nodes.label: Four Layer-2 Language Philosophies

nodes.label: Mina / Coda

nodes.label: Proof-Carrying Data (PCD)

nodes.label: Recursion Gap
nodes.rationale: The multiplicative overhead of proving a verifier versus just running it; levers include smaller fields, better in-circuit hashes, lookups, and folding's near-elimination of the embedded verifier.

nodes.label: SBOM Verification as PCD

nodes.rationale: The verifier circuit must be asymptotically and concretely smaller than the statements proven or recursion diverges; accumulation and folding deliberately relax this by deferring expensive checks.

nodes.label: Allspice
nodes.rationale: Uses static analysis to choose per computation between the non-cryptographic CMT-derived protocols (CMT-slim, CMT-batching) and the cryptographic Zaatar/Ginger argument systems, because neither approach dominates: CMT avoids expensive cryptography but requires highly regular circuits, while batching amortizes cryptographic costs only in data-parallel settings.

nodes.label: Quadratic Span Program
nodes.rationale: A new characterization of NP built to construct succinct arguments without PCP machinery: where Groth10 and Lipmaa12 had quadratic prover computation, QSPs give a 7-group-element NIZK with linear CRS size and quasi-linear prover work.

nodes.label: Square Span Program (SSP)
nodes.rationale: Every 2-input binary gate becomes an affine combination that takes exactly the values {0,2} when the gate is respected, i.e. a single square constraint (l-1)^2 = 1. Using one series of polynomials instead of QSP's two or QAP's three shrinks the setup, keys, and proofs: 4 group elements verified in 6 pairings (est. 160-byte proofs verified in under 6 ms), at the cost of binary rather than arithmetic circuits.

nodes.label: Subversion Zero-Knowledge
nodes.rationale: Since subversion soundness and standard zero-knowledge are mutually impossible (Bellare et al.), the updatable CRS model targets the achievable middle ground: subversion/updatable zero-knowledge together with updatable soundness.

nodes.label: Updatable Common Reference String
nodes.rationale: A middle ground between fully trusted and fully subverted CRS models: any user may update the CRS with a proof of correct update, and the result is sound as long as at least one updater in the sequence was honest.

nodes.label: Updatable Universal Structured Reference String
nodes.rationale: An updatable SRS lets an open, dynamic set of participants contribute secret randomness indefinitely; security holds if any single updater was honest, mitigating trusted-setup risk without discarding SNARK efficiency, and a universal SRS removes per-circuit re-setup.

nodes.rationale: A circuit whose polynomial constraints admit multiple witnesses for the same input, letting a malicious prover generate bogus proofs the verifier accepts; the root cause of several multimillion-dollar blockchain exploits such as the TornadoCash hack, and the central bug class both QED2 and ZKAP target.
