nodes.label: On-the-Fly Degree Two Elimination
nodes.rationale: Eliminates degree-two elements almost instantly without relation gathering or linear algebra, and the descent built from it removes smoothness assumptions about non-uniformly distributed polynomials, making the quasi-polynomial algorithm practical at viable bitlengths and better suited to theoretical analysis.

nodes.label: Pairing-Based Cryptosystem Key Sizes
nodes.rationale: exTNFS lowers the asymptotic complexity of discrete logarithms in F_p^n for composite extension degrees (n=6, n=12), which forces larger key sizes for the associated pairing-based cryptosystems such as those over Barreto-Naehrig curves.

nodes.label: libiop Library
nodes.rationale: C++ library for writing IOP-based arguments: a toolchain of transformations lets programmers compose new arguments from simple IOP sub-components; used to specify Aurora and prior constructions.

nodes.label: Univariate Sumcheck Protocol
nodes.rationale: New IOP verifying the sum of entries of a Reed-Solomon codeword over any subgroup of a field — a univariate analogue of the classical LFKN sumcheck for multivariate polynomials, and the key ingredient of Aurora.

nodes.label: Recursive Amortization
nodes.rationale: LaBRADOR stands for Lattice-Based Recursively Amortized Demonstration Of R1CS: repeated amortized self-reduction compresses the proof instead of a single-shot PCP compilation.

nodes.label: Holographic Proof
nodes.rationale: The verifier queries an encoding of the circuit instead of reading it, enabling sublinear verification for arbitrary circuits; Fractal's holographic IOP for R1CS is the first with efficient indexer, prover, and verifier.

nodes.label: Preprocessing SNARK
nodes.rationale: Offline phase produces a short circuit summary; online verification runs polylogarithmic in circuit size. Recursive composition is simpler for preprocessing SNARKs — the observation Fractal's methodology starts from.

nodes.label: Recursive Proof Composition
nodes.rationale: Producing a SNARK about a computation that validates prior SNARKs; requires an argument of knowledge, and prior to Fractal the only efficient approach used pairing-based SNARKs on MNT curve cycles (pre-quantum, trusted setup, expensive algebra).

nodes.label: Ben-Sasson et al., Aurora: Transparent Succinct Arguments for R1CS (EUROCRYPT 2019)
nodes.norm_label: ben-sasson et al., aurora: transparent succinct arguments for r1cs (eurocrypt 2019)
nodes.rationale: zkSNARG for R1CS with transparent setup, plausible post-quantum security, and lightweight (hash-based) cryptography: O(log^2 n) proof size, O(n log n) prover, proofs under 250 kB at 128-bit security for millions of constraints.

nodes.label: Chiesa-Ojha-Spooner, Fractal: Post-Quantum and Transparent Recursive Proofs from Holography (EUROCRYPT 2020)
nodes.norm_label: chiesa-ojha-spooner, fractal: post-quantum and transparent recursive proofs from holography (eurocrypt 2020)
nodes.rationale: First efficient recursive SNARK composition that is post-quantum and transparent, avoiding pairing-friendly curve cycles: holographic IOPs compile to preprocessing SNARGs in the (quantum) random oracle model, and a SNARK verifier for 2M constraints fits in 1.7M constraints, enabling arbitrary recursion depth.

nodes.label: Cyclic Lattices
nodes.rationale: Lattices closed under cyclic coordinate rotation, intimately connected to the ring Z[a]/(a^n - 1); the factorization of a^n - 1 into cyclotomic polynomials is what the security proof exploits.

nodes.label: Discrete Gaussian Distribution Bound
nodes.rationale: New bound on the discrete Gaussian over general lattices, built on Micciancio-Regev Gaussian-measure techniques.

nodes.label: Generalized Knapsack Function
nodes.rationale: f_a(x) = sum a_i * x_i over a ring R with coefficients from S subset of R; the choice of S is what separates mere one-wayness from collision resistance.

nodes.label: Linear-Time Encodable Code
nodes.rationale: Core ingredient distilled from BCG's polynomial commitment; existing constructions (Spielman, Druk-Ishai) were believed impractical, so Brakedown designs and engineers a new practical one.

nodes.label: Shockwave (Reed-Solomon Brakedown Variant)
nodes.rationale: Trades linear-time proving for Reed-Solomon codes: shorter proofs and lower verification than Brakedown, and a faster prover than prior plausibly post-quantum SNARKs.

nodes.label: Ligero (Ames-Hazay-Ishai-Venkitasubramaniam, CCS 2017)
nodes.rationale: Lightweight sublinear argument without trusted setup; the PCP-type hash-based baseline (with Aurora and Shockwave) that LaBRADOR's lattice proofs beat on size.

nodes.label: AVX-512 Ring Arithmetic Library
nodes.rationale: Optimized library for small-degree power-of-two cyclotomic rings modulo multi-precision primes q = 5 mod 8, with multi-modular NTT representations, ring automorphisms, and a Four-Russians Johnson-Lindenstrauss implementation.

nodes.label: Inner/Outer Commitment Structure
nodes.rationale: Two-layer Ajtai-style commitments from LaBRADOR: inner commitments t_i = A G^-1(f_i) are decomposed and re-committed via an outer commitment u = B(t-hat), so the whole verification condition becomes one lattice-type linear relation provable by LaBRADOR.

nodes.label: Approximate (Relaxed) Zero-Knowledge Proofs
nodes.rationale: Fiat-Shamir-style lattice proofs extract f(s-bar) = c-bar * t with a relaxation factor c-bar rather than the original witness; applications (commitments, verifiable encryption, voting) stay sound only if c-bar is invertible in the ring.

nodes.label: Challenge Set Invertibility
nodes.rationale: Lattice ZK challenge sets must be large (~2^256), have small norm, and have all non-zero differences invertible; the third property is what previously forced efficiency compromises in ring choice.

nodes.label: Partially Splitting Cyclotomic Rings
nodes.rationale: Choosing the prime p so X^n+1 splits into k irreducible factors trades NTT multiplication speed against invertibility of small elements; sufficient congruence conditions on p (e.g. p = 2k+1 mod 4k) guarantee the desired factorization.

nodes.label: Module Lattices
nodes.rationale: Bridge between arbitrary lattices and ideal lattices; worst-case hardness on this class backs Module-SIS/Module-LWE.

nodes.label: Module-LWE
nodes.rationale: Average-case problem interpolating between LWE and Ring-LWE; enlarges the lattice cryptographer's toolbox with a tunable structure/security trade-off.

nodes.label: Ring-SIS / Ring-LWE
nodes.rationale: Compact ring variants of SIS/LWE whose hardness rests only on ideal-lattice restrictions — the security weakening that motivates the module generalization.

nodes.label: Monomial Challenges
nodes.rationale: Challenges of the form X^i in Z[X]/(X^d+1) give a 2d-size challenge space where doubled inverses of challenge differences have small norm; analyzed for (k+1)-special-sound protocols and avoiding special-form moduli so NTT still applies.

nodes.label: One-out-of-Many Proof
nodes.rationale: Prove knowledge of an opening of one commitment within a set without revealing which; with Fiat-Shamir this directly yields ring signatures where public keys are commitments to secret keys.

nodes.label: Ring Signature
nodes.rationale: Anonymity tool for e-voting and cryptocurrencies; extendable to linkable variants for confidential transactions.

nodes.label: Soundness Gap (Relaxed Extraction)
nodes.rationale: The extractor recovers openings of gamma * Com(m; r) instead of the actual commitments — a lattice-specific complication absent from discrete-log protocols that the unforgeability proof must handle.

nodes.label: Peikert-Rosen, Efficient Collision-Resistant Hashing from Worst-Case Assumptions on Cyclic Lattices (TCC 2006)
nodes.norm_label: peikert-rosen, efficient collision-resistant hashing from worst-case assumptions on cyclic lattices (tcc 2006)
nodes.rationale: Shows the generalized knapsack function is collision-resistant for a different coefficient subset S, assuming worst-case hardness of approximating SVP on cyclic lattices; yields hash functions with key size and time almost linear in the security parameter, and proves Micciancio's original choice is not collision-resistant.

nodes.label: Bootle-Chiesa-Groth, Linear-Time Arguments from Tensor Codes (TCC 2020)
nodes.norm_label: bootle-chiesa-groth, linear-time arguments from tensor codes (tcc 2020)

nodes.label: Golovnev-Lee-Setty-Thaler-Wahby, Brakedown: Linear-Time and Field-Agnostic SNARKs for R1CS (CRYPTO 2023)
nodes.norm_label: golovnev-lee-setty-thaler-wahby, brakedown: linear-time and field-agnostic snarks for r1cs (crypto 2023)
nodes.rationale: First built SNARK with a linear-time O(N) prover for R1CS; no trusted setup, plausibly post-quantum, and compatible with arbitrary sufficiently large finite fields. Obtained by combining the BCG (TCC 2020) polynomial commitment with Spartan's linear-time interactive proof.

nodes.label: Beullens-Seiler, LaBRADOR: Compact Proofs for R1CS from Module-SIS (CRYPTO 2023)
nodes.norm_label: beullens-seiler, labrador: compact proofs for r1cs from module-sis (crypto 2023)
nodes.rationale: First lattice-based proof system more compact than hash-based PCP-type systems: 58 KB proofs for R1CS mod 2^64+1 with 2^20 constraints at 128-bit security, an order of magnitude smaller than previous quantum-safe proofs, by allowing the stronger Module-SIS assumption.

nodes.label: Nguyen-Seiler, Greyhound: Fast Polynomial Commitments from Lattices (CRYPTO 2024)
nodes.norm_label: nguyen-seiler, greyhound: fast polynomial commitments from lattices (crypto 2024)
nodes.rationale: First concretely efficient polynomial commitment from standard lattice assumptions (Module-SIS): a three-round evaluation protocol composed with LaBRADOR yields polylog(N) proofs (53 KB at N=2^30) with sublinear verification and transparent setup.

nodes.label: Lyubashevsky-Seiler, Short Invertible Elements in Partially Splitting Cyclotomic Rings (EUROCRYPT 2018)
nodes.norm_label: lyubashevsky-seiler, short invertible elements in partially splitting cyclotomic rings (eurocrypt 2018)
nodes.rationale: Proves all non-zero small-coefficient polynomials in Z_p[X]/(Phi_m(X)) are invertible when p is chosen so the cyclotomic splits into a bounded number of factors — letting lattice ZK proofs keep optimal sparse ±1 challenge sets while X^n+1 splits into 8-16 factors, giving a free 2-3x NTT speedup.

nodes.label: Langlois-Stehlé, Worst-Case to Average-Case Reductions for Module Lattices (Des. Codes Cryptogr. 2015)
nodes.norm_label: langlois-stehle, worst-case to average-case reductions for module lattices (des. codes cryptogr. 2015)
nodes.rationale: Defines Module-SIS and Module-LWE, bridging SIS with Ring-SIS and LWE with Ring-LWE, and proves them at least as hard as worst-case problems on module lattices; unlike the ring setting the reductions are qualitatively sharp (converse reductions exist).

nodes.label: Esgin et al., Short Lattice-Based One-out-of-Many Proofs and Applications to Ring Signatures (ACNS 2019)
nodes.norm_label: esgin et al., short lattice-based one-out-of-many proofs and applications to ring signatures (acns 2019)
nodes.rationale: Resolves the open problem of extending Groth-Kohlweiss/Bootle-style one-out-of-many proofs to lattices: log-size proofs and a ring signature of 3 MB at ring size one billion (vs. 216 MB prior), the first lattice ZKP instantiated on Module-SIS to trade extracted-witness growth against speed.

nodes.label: Bilinear pairing e(g^x, g^y) = e(g,g)^xy
nodes.rationale: Lets a verifier check product relationships in the exponent without computing them, which is exactly what KZG and BLS verification need.

nodes.label: KZG polynomial commitment (Kate-Zaverucha-Goldberg 2010)
nodes.rationale: Constant-size commitment g^f(tau) and single-group-element proof g^q(tau) from the identity f(X)-f(u)=(X-u)q(X), verified with one pairing at the secret tau; sound under q-strong bilinear Diffie-Hellman plus knowledge-of-exponent or the generic group model; supports batch openings, Lagrange-basis linear-time commitment, and multivariate/ZK variants; drawback: trusted setup and linear-size parameters.

nodes.label: Trusted setup ceremony (distributed powers-of-tau)
nodes.rationale: Each contributor rerandomizes gp by powers of its secret s, proving knowledge of s and preserving the consecutive-powers structure (checked via pairings); secure if at least one participant discards their secret.

nodes.label: SNARK setup modes (per-circuit trusted, universal, transparent)
nodes.norm_label: snark setup modes (per-circuit trusted, universal, transparent)
nodes.rationale: Per-circuit trusted setup is worst (Groth16): leaked randomness lets a prover forge proofs, so ceremony machines must be destroyed; universal setup (Plonk/Marlin) runs one ceremony for all circuits; transparent setup (Bulletproofs, STARK) needs no secrets at all.

nodes.label: Knowledge soundness (extractor definition)
nodes.rationale: If an adversary convinces the verifier, an extractor interacting with it recovers a valid witness with essentially the same probability; SNARGs drop this requirement.

nodes.label: Schwartz-Zippel-DeMillo-Lipton lemma
nodes.rationale: A nonzero (multivariate) polynomial of total degree d vanishes at a random point with probability at most d/p, giving the random-evaluation zero/equality test that makes SNARKs possible.

nodes.label: SNARK (succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge)
nodes.rationale: Proof must be sublinear in witness size and verification sublinear in circuit size; strongly succinct in practice means logarithmic (often constant) proof size and verify time, which forces a preprocessing step that summarizes the circuit for the verifier.

nodes.label: Arkworks R1CS constraint library (Rust)
nodes.rationale: Circuit-synthesis library embedded in Rust: full host-language expressiveness for witness computation and gadget abstraction, but the developer hand-optimizes constraint count.

nodes.label: Circom (hardware description language for R1CS)
nodes.rationale: Direct constraint control: <-- assigns witness values, === creates rank-1 constraints, <== does both; elegant and explicit but hard to learn and weak on abstraction (only sub-circuits, no types).

nodes.label: R1CS (rank-1 constraint system)
nodes.rationale: Predicate as constraints alpha*beta=gamma over affine combinations, equivalently matrices A,B,C with Az o Bz = Cz; the assembly language of ZKPs that HDLs, libraries and compilers all target.

nodes.label: ZoKrates (ZKP programming language and compiler)
nodes.rationale: Easiest to learn with familiar PL semantics, but gives up control: witnesses cannot be computed during execution and must arrive as main-function arguments.

nodes.label: Sum-check-based polynomial IOP for circuit satisfiability
nodes.norm_label: sum-check-based polynomial iop for circuit satisfiability
nodes.rationale: Prover commits to an extension h of the circuit transcript; a derived polynomial g_h built from add/mult wiring predicates vanishes on the hypercube iff the transcript is correct; checked by sum-check instead of quotient polynomials, avoiding large FFTs and extra committed polynomials.

nodes.label: Multilinear extension
nodes.rationale: Unique multilinear polynomial agreeing with f on the hypercube; a distance-amplified encoding - functions differing at one input have extensions differing almost everywhere - and evaluable from f's table in O(2^l) time via Lagrange interpolation.

nodes.label: Sum-check protocol (Lund-Fortnow-Karloff-Nisan)
nodes.rationale: Verifier offloads summing an l-variate polynomial over the Boolean hypercube: one round per variable, O(d*l) communication, a single oracle query at the end; soundness error d*l/|F|; prover runs in near-optimal time.

nodes.label: Accumulation Scheme
nodes.rationale: Instead of verifying a SNARK at every IVC step, verification checks are accumulated; the recursive statement only ensures accumulation was performed correctly, which is far cheaper.

nodes.label: Complexity-Preserving SNARK
nodes.rationale: Motivated by prover space being the practical bottleneck: bootstrapping via recursive composition removes expensive preprocessing and keeps prover time and space close to what classical NP verification requires.

nodes.label: Inner Sumcheck Aggregation
nodes.rationale: Aggregating Marlin's inner sumchecks across the nodes of a recursive scheme (adapting Halo's strategy for bivariate circuit polynomials) cuts recursive prover cost by roughly 30% in a tree of in-degree 2, at the cost of about tripling proof size.

nodes.label: Nested Amortization
nodes.rationale: Instead of a fully succinct verifier circuit, linear-time commitment-opening checks are deferred as public inputs and collapsed across recursion depth with an untrusted helper, so the expensive check is performed only once at the end of the recursive chain.

nodes.label: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC)

nodes.label: CycleFold EC Co-Processor Circuit
nodes.rationale: Delegates the folding verifier's few scalar multiplications to a tiny (about 1,000-1,500 multiplication gate) circuit over the second curve's scalar field, avoiding non-native field emulation; the resulting second-curve circuit is nearly an order of magnitude smaller than the BCTV14-style verifier circuit used in Nova's 2-cycle implementation, and neither the IVC construction nor its security proof must reason about the curve cycle.

nodes.label: 2-Cycle Nova Soundness Vulnerability
nodes.rationale: The original 2-cycle Nova implementation's IVC proof contained an extra R1CS instance-witness pair insufficiently constrained by the verifier, allowing a forged proof of 2^75 rounds of the Minroot VDF in 1.46 seconds; the fix eliminates that pair, yielding shorter IVC proofs with a formal knowledge-soundness proof, and the paper also shows Nova IVC proofs are malleable.

nodes.label: Split Accumulation Scheme
nodes.rationale: Introduced because requiring succinct arguments (or even atomic succinct accumulation) for PCD is unnecessarily strong; letting the accumulation verifier see only short instance parts while witnesses stay large yields simpler, cheaper recursion and enables PCD from non-succinct NARKs with a constant-size accumulation verifier.
